samples.summary: Imports a `pin` export that does not exist anywhere in the repo, so the module cannot load at all
samples.evidence: `import { assertComparableWindow, assertOnePopulation, pin } from "./volume-mix.mjs";` — `volume-mix.mjs` contains no word-boundary occurrence of `pin` (only `pinned`/prose), and a repo-wide search for an exported `pin` finds none: it exists only as a PRIVATE 2-arg const in `complementarity.mjs:77` and `report.mjs:81` (`const pin = (what, ok) => …`). validity.mjs also calls it with three arguments (`pin("joined", JOIN_STATUSES, "the joinable status")`), a signature no existing copy has. An ESM named import that the target module does not provide is a load-time error, so neither the CLI nor `validity.test.mjs` can run. (The scripts/agent node:test lane would catch this, but it means the change as submitted cannot deliver the metric at all.)

samples.summary: New scorer is not registered in `score-all.mjs` STEPS or `report.mjs` SECTIONS, so its payload cannot be filed and never reaches the deliverable comparison report
samples.evidence: `report.mjs:1538` refuses `--persist --scorer-id validity-v1` outright (`SCORER_IDS` is derived from `SECTIONS`, which lists only volume-mix/complementarity/reliability/cost-latency/segmentation), and `score-all.mjs:86 STEPS` — the driver the CI scoring lane runs — has no validity step. The result is a scorer whose figures exist only on one operator's stderr: nothing filed under `scores/`, nothing rendered. Meanwhile `report.mjs:980-983` still tells every reader "There is no precision figure, no recall figure and no correctness figure anywhere in this document", and `report.mjs:1377` "No adjudicated labels exist" — text that the report cannot update because the section does not exist. The file's own header ("adds no report section") suggests this is deliberate staging, so the acceptance criteria may or may not require it; flagging because spec §4's deliverable is the rendered comparison, not a stderr dump.

samples.summary: Re-declares the renderer's existing availability vocabulary with a renamed state instead of importing it, so cells cannot be handed to `renderCell` without translation
samples.evidence: `report.mjs:186` already exports `AVAILABILITY = ["present", "not-computed", "not-measurable", "suppressed"]` with `renderCell`/`notMeasurable`/`suppressed` helpers built on it, and `renderCell` REFUSES any cell whose `availability` is outside that list (`report.mjs:253-254`). validity.mjs defines its own `AVAILABILITY = ["reported", "suppressed", "not-computed", "not-measurable"]` — the same four-state concept with `present` renamed to `reported` — and every cell it emits carries `availability: "reported"`, which the renderer would reject. This is exactly the duplication-with-drift the repo's own comments ("a second copy here is how a caption comes to contradict its own table") argue against; either import the vocabulary or state why the two differ.

samples.summary: No design/doc update for a new scorer, new score id and three new vocabularies; the subsystem README's module table is left claiming the remaining scorers are not built
samples.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 and :58-60 require a feature/non-trivial change to write or update a design doc, folding into the canonical subsystem doc. The canonical doc for this directory is `scripts/agent/eval/README.md`, whose "What exists today" table ends at `volume-mix.mjs` ("the first scorer") and states at lines 30-32 that "the remaining scorers — complementarity, reliability, cost and latency — are not built yet." This diff adds a sixth scorer with a new `scorer_id`, a four-state availability vocabulary, a five-state join vocabulary, a claim-population vocabulary and two permanently refused metrics, and documents none of it outside the module's own header comment. (The README was already stale for reliability/segmentation/adjudicate/labels, so this compounds rather than starts the drift.)

samples.summary: Relative recall bypasses the existing cross-arm matching lane, producing a band `[a/(a+b), a/max(a,b)]` wide enough to be uninformative
samples.evidence: `complementarity.mjs` already owns cross-arm class matching and band arithmetic (`VIEWS` incl. `union`, label-resolved vs unlabelled bands, `both_upper_bound`), and `finding-match.mjs` is the repo's designated "same defect, said differently" mechanism (README.md:586). validity.mjs deliberately reimplements a union bound from set theory alone and imports neither. That is defensible while pair labels are unresolved, but it means the metric spec §3.3 asks for is emitted at a width no reader can act on (on the pilot's shape, panel 6 vs CodeRabbit 30 gives [0.167, 0.200]) while an existing module holds the matched classes that would narrow it. Approach/layer preference rather than an unmet criterion.

samples.summary: CLI `--arm` filters the claim population but not the labels, so a scoped run reports a whole arm as `claims-not-supplied`
samples.evidence: `main()` builds `arms` only for the selected arm(s) but always reads every label via `readFindingLabels(root, corpusVersion)`. With `--arm panel`, every CodeRabbit label lands in the `claims-not-supplied` join bucket and the payload carries a full arm with no denominators — the exact "wrong census rather than a missing one" state the module's own JOIN_STATUSES prose warns about. Either filter labels by the selected arm(s) or refuse the combination.

samples.summary: `stated-severity-varies` widens a severity-keyed census with a value outside `KNOWN` without declaring it in a shared vocabulary
samples.evidence: `distinct_keys_by_stated_severity` is keyed by `KNOWN` plus the local string `STATED_SEVERITY_VARIES`, and a claim's `severity` field is overwritten with that string. Any consumer iterating `KNOWN` over this map silently drops the bucket, and any consumer reading `claim.severity` as a scale value now sees an off-scale token. The concept is right; it belongs in a declared, exported vocabulary the way `WINDOW`/`gating` are, rather than as a module-private constant.

verdict.reason: The claimed missing export exists: `volume-mix.mjs:63` declares `export function pin(value, vocabulary, what)`, a 3-parameter exported function, used in-file with three arguments at lines 75/78/80 and imported+tested by `volume-mix.test.mjs:41,133-140`. `validity.mjs:77`'s named import of `{ assertComparableWindow, assertOnePopulation, pin }` therefore resolves (the other two are exported at `volume-mix.mjs:756` and `:788`), and its 3-arg call at `validity.mjs:192` matches the exported signature exactly. finding.summary: New scorer is not registered in `score-all.mjs` STEPS or `report.mjs` SECTIONS, so its payload cannot be filed and never reaches the deliverable comparison report
finding.evidence: `report.mjs:1538` refuses `--persist --scorer-id validity-v1` outright (`SCORER_IDS` is derived from `SECTIONS`, which lists only volume-mix/complementarity/reliability/cost-latency/segmentation), and `score-all.mjs:86 STEPS` — the driver the CI scoring lane runs — has no validity step. The result is a scorer whose figures exist only on one operator's stderr: nothing filed under `scores/`, nothing rendered. Meanwhile `report.mjs:980-983` still tells every reader "There is no precision figure, no recall figure and no correctness figure anywhere in this document", and `report.mjs:1377` "No adjudicated labels exist" — text that the report cannot update because the section does not exist. The file's own header ("adds no report section") suggests this is deliberate staging, so the acceptance criteria may or may not require it; flagging because spec §4's deliverable is the rendered comparison, not a stderr dump.

verdict.reason: The absence is factually real — validity-v1 appears in no SECTIONS/SCORER_IDS entry (report.mjs:109-119), no STEPS entry (score-all.mjs:86-92), and nowhere in .github/workflows — so there is no counterexample. It is nevertheless not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) It is the change's own explicitly stated non-goal, with a named follow-up: docs/tasks/active/20260820-eval-validity-scorer-todo.md:157-158 ("No report section … rendering validity-v1 is a follow-up") and :166 ("Nothing is persisted. Like every merged scorer here it reads, computes and prints"). Conforming to a stated Non-Goal is not a fit violation; only exceeding one is. This is the repo's established staging pattern — docs/tasks/active/20260812-eval-adjudication-cli-todo.md:318-319 landed the label store with "No metric … a scorer over labels is a later change", and score-all.mjs itself arrived in a separate later task (20260813-eval-scoring-lane). (b) Registering it now would actively break the lane: report.mjs:1626-1649 sets exitCode 1 for any SECTIONS entry with no filed score, and score-all.mjs:590/620 refuse the pass on any non-zero exit, while the task doc's measured real-store run (lines 186-194) shows validity legitimately exits 1 / PARTIAL because no adjudicated labels exist yet. So the requested wiring would red every CI scoring pass. (c) The finding's corroborating evidence is incorrect: report.mjs:980-983 ("no precision figure … anywhere in this document") stays accurate exactly because no validity section renders, so no contradictory text is introduced. What remains is a staging/scope preference — minor at most, not an unmet acceptance criterion the reviewer can name.

finding.summary: Re-declares the renderer's existing availability vocabulary with a renamed state instead of importing it, so cells cannot be handed to `renderCell` without translation
finding.evidence: `report.mjs:186` already exports `AVAILABILITY = ["present", "not-computed", "not-measurable", "suppressed"]` with `renderCell`/`notMeasurable`/`suppressed` helpers built on it, and `renderCell` REFUSES any cell whose `availability` is outside that list (`report.mjs:253-254`). validity.mjs defines its own `AVAILABILITY = ["reported", "suppressed", "not-computed", "not-measurable"]` — the same four-state concept with `present` renamed to `reported` — and every cell it emits carries `availability: "reported"`, which the renderer would reject. This is exactly the duplication-with-drift the repo's own comments ("a second copy here is how a caption comes to contradict its own table") argue against; either import the vocabulary or state why the two differ.

verdict.reason: The literals exist as quoted, but the premise that a scorer must reuse report.mjs's AVAILABILITY is contradicted by the repo's own layering. report.mjs's AVAILABILITY is a renderer-internal *cell* vocabulary produced only by report's own constructors (figure :200, notComputed :212, notMeasurable :220, suppressed :234); no scorer emits it and no scorer imports report.mjs (dependency runs renderer -> scorers; score-all.mjs:46 is the only importer, for comparisonIdFor). The established pattern is scorer-owned vocabularies that report translates: segmentation-v1 emits `suppressed: true/false` and report.mjs:822 converts it (`c.suppressed === true ? suppressed(...) : figure(...)`); pair-labels.mjs:191 owns a seven-state LABEL_AVAILABILITY with completely different names, documented as "pair-labels.mjs owns the vocabulary", which the renderer maps via LABEL_CAUSE plus an import-time pin (.trusted/scripts/agent/eval/report.mjs:471-490, :572). So "cells cannot be handed to renderCell without translation" is true of every scorer and is the intended seam, not duplication-with-drift. On top of that, the originating issue lists "No report section ... rendering validity-v1 is a follow-up" as an explicit non-goal (docs/tasks/active/20260820-eval-validity-scorer-todo.md:157-158), and validity.mjs renders its own output for "reported" (:966, :984-1015) while deriving its states from denominators/claim populations via availabilityFor (:348) — a different concept from report's presentation states, documented at validity.mjs:120-140. Not a blocking design-fit defect.
